A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FLOCK and provide readable text, figures, tables, equations and appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original PETALS experiments, entity and relation prediction results across 54 knowledge graphs, ablations and scalability measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds component ablations, a PETALS noise-control experiment, embedding visualizations and a correlation analysis.

M1.justification: The proposed sampler, anonymization, GRU processor, weighted consensus, walk-count adaptation and training losses are retained. The transformer and altered sampling configurations are experimental ablations, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: PETALS, the 54-KG evaluation suite, entity/relation prediction tasks and pretraining graph mixes remain unchanged. The new studies reuse METAFAM or subsets of the existing benchmarks.

E2.justification: v2 Table 8c adds TRIX with noise to the PETALS comparison; v1 evaluated that comparator only on the broader KG prediction tasks. The existing ULTRA, MOTIF and TRIX comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New study protocols include controlled component ablations on 41 inductive and five transductive KGs, METAFAM embedding PCA, and analysis of MRR ratios against log-density on 53 KGs. Established benchmark splits, ranking metrics and listed training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 expands beyond adaptive walk counts to test backtracking, walk length, starting locations, GRU versus transformer, and weighted consensus. v2 also adds the PETALS noise control, METAFAM embedding case study and graph-density analysis, substantially broadening diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Figure 7 and Appendix H introduce a Pearson correlation significance test and report p = 5.0e-5. Neither version reports training-seed variability or confidence intervals for benchmark scores; the existing stochastic inference ensembling is retained.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark and scalability values match. Substantial new results include Table 5's 46-KG MRR of 0.395 for FLOCK versus 0.359 for its transformer variant, 52% PETALS accuracy for TRIX with noise, METAFAM embedding separation, and correlation r = -0.53 between relative MRR and log-density.

T1.justification: Definitions, Propositions 4.1–4.3, PETALS construction, complexity bounds and detailed proofs are retained after matching v1 Appendix C to v2 Appendix B. The added main-text proof sketches summarize arguments already present in v1.

C1.justification: The novelty claim is narrowed from introducing probabilistic node-relation equivariance to applying that principle, consistent with v2's explicit acknowledgment of prior stochastic KGFMs. Claims about FLOCK's universality, PETALS performance and 54-KG evaluation remain.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's general coverage hypothesis, v2 develops explanations involving METAFAM relation-embedding collapse, graph density and edge-cover time, coverage versus sequence learnability, and GRU efficiency under small parameter budgets. It also identifies expressivity with restricted walk lengths as an open question.

D1.justification: v2 updates the advertised repository from flock-pytorch to flock and adds a reproducibility statement specifying training/evaluation scripts, pretrained checkpoints and a PETALS generator. Hardware disclosures and detailed hyperparameter tables are retained; the PDFs do not establish a change in the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: v1's 'first stochastic KGFM' positioning is replaced by acknowledgment of stochastic InGram/ISDEA and a distinction based on FLOCK's random-walk architecture. Supporting references on non-backtracking mixing, transformers, reconstruction, scalable walks and edge-cover time are added.

P1.justification: v2 extensively edits the abstract, introduction and related work, expands methodological explanations and reorganizes the experimental narrative. Appendices change from PETALS–method–proofs to method–proofs–PETALS, and ethics and reproducibility statements are added.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5 and Figures 6–7, expands the noise-comparison table with a PETALS panel, and consolidates v1 Tables 8–15 into four combined benchmark tables. Retained figures and tables are also resized or relocated, substantially changing visual organization.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's limited component validation, v2's ablations and PETALS noise control provide useful evidence for architectural choices, while revised novelty claims better acknowledge prior stochastic KGFMs. These strengthen the paper, although the new PCA/correlation explanations remain suggestive and performance comparisons still lack run-to-run uncertainty reporting.
